Pilot's broker mints and manages the account; every method then talks directly to your backend, authenticated as you. Free to provision — pay only for what your backend uses.

methods.name: insforge.signup
methods.description: Provision your OWN isolated InsForge backend in ONE call — no email, no browser, no human step. This signs a keyless request to Pilot's InsForge signup broker, which mints a fresh InsForge project under Pilot's managed account and returns its access key + backend URL. The adapter caches {api_key, backend_url} to $APP/secrets.json, and from then on EVERY other insforge.* method talks directly to YOUR backend, authenticated as you. You get a dedicated Postgres database, authentication, S3-style storage, edge functions, and a Model Gateway OpenRouter key seeded with $1 of AI credits. Idempotent: the broker provisions at most one project per Pilot identity, so a repeat call (or a fresh install) returns the SAME backend. Run this ONCE before any other method. FREE to provision — you pay only for the resources your backend actually uses (see per-method costs and insforge.help). Retrieve your backend URL + key any time via insforge.account. Takes no arguments.

methods.name: insforge.account
methods.description: Retrieve your provisioned InsForge backend — its backend_url, your api_key, and project id — plus a signed_up flag. Local, instant, FREE (reads $APP/secrets.json; no backend call). Use it to confirm you're provisioned or to read your key/URL (e.g. to call the backend from your own code). If signed_up is false, call insforge.signup first.

methods.name: insforge.metadata
methods.description: Get your backend's full configuration — auth providers/SMTP, database tables, storage buckets, edge functions, realtime, and AI models — in one call. FREE (control-plane / metadata).

methods.name: insforge.db_list_tables
methods.description: List all database tables with their schemas (columns, types, constraints). FREE (control-plane / metadata).

methods.name: insforge.db_create_table
methods.description: Create a Postgres table. Body: {tableName, columns:[{columnName, type, isNullable, isUnique, defaultValue?}]} — type is one of string, integer, float, boolean, datetime, date, uuid, json. An id (uuid) + createdAt/updatedAt are added automatically. Rows count toward Postgres storage (500 MB free, then $0.125/GB); reads toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

methods.name: insforge.db_query
methods.description: Query records from a table with PostgREST-style filtering, sorting, pagination. Path: table name. Query params: limit (1-1000, default 100), offset, order (e.g. createdAt.desc), select (comma columns), and any {field}=<op>.<value> filter (op: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, ilike, in, is). Counts toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

methods.name: insforge.db_insert
methods.description: Insert one or more records into a table. Path: table name. Body: a JSON array of row objects (e.g. [{"title":"hi"}]) — always an array, even for one row. Returns the inserted rows with generated ids. Note: just after db_create_table, wait ~3s before the first insert (the database reloads its schema cache after DDL; an immediate insert can 404). Rows count toward Postgres storage (500 MB free, then $0.125/GB); reads toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

params.name: records
params.description: Array of row objects to insert (sent as the request body).

methods.name: insforge.db_update
methods.description: Update records matching PostgREST filters. Path: table name. Pass filter(s) as query params ({field}=eq.<value>) and the new column values in the body. Returns the updated rows. Rows count toward Postgres storage (500 MB free, then $0.125/GB); reads toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

methods.name: insforge.db_delete
methods.description: Delete records matching PostgREST filters. Path: table name. Pass filter(s) as query params ({field}=eq.<value>). Returns the deleted rows. Rows count toward Postgres storage (500 MB free, then $0.125/GB); reads toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

methods.name: insforge.db_sql
methods.description: Run raw parameterized SQL against your Postgres database. Body: {query, params?}. Powerful — use for joins, aggregates, DDL, migrations. Rows count toward Postgres storage (500 MB free, then $0.125/GB); reads toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

methods.name: insforge.storage_list_buckets
methods.description: List your storage buckets. FREE (control-plane / metadata).

methods.name: insforge.storage_create_bucket
methods.description: Create a storage bucket. Body: {bucketName, isPublic}. A public bucket serves objects without auth; a private one requires the key. FREE (control-plane / metadata).

params.name: isPublic
params.description: Public (no-auth reads) if true; default false.

methods.name: insforge.storage_list_objects
methods.description: List objects in a bucket (paginated). Path: bucket name. Query: limit, offset, prefix. Counts toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

methods.name: insforge.storage_download
methods.description: Download an object (returns its content). Path: bucket + object key. Counts toward bandwidth (5 GB free, then $0.09/GB).

methods.name: insforge.storage_delete
methods.description: Delete an object. Path: bucket + object key. FREE (control-plane / metadata).

methods.name: insforge.auth_config
methods.description: Get your backend's auth configuration (enabled OAuth providers, JWT settings, SMTP). FREE (control-plane / metadata).

methods.name: insforge.auth_list_users
methods.description: List the end-users registered in your backend's auth (paginated). Query: limit, offset. Auth users count toward MAU (50,000 free, then $0.00325 per monthly active user).

methods.name: insforge.functions_list
methods.description: List your deployed edge functions (Deno/TypeScript) and the runtime status. FREE (control-plane / metadata).

methods.name: insforge.function_invoke
methods.description: Invoke a deployed edge function by slug. Path: function slug. Body: the JSON payload passed to the function. Each invocation counts toward edge-function calls (100,000 free, then $0.01 per 1,000).

methods.name: insforge.ai_gateway_key
methods.description: Get your project's Model Gateway OpenRouter API key (sk-or-...). InsForge provisions it seeded with $1 of AI credits; call it directly against https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with any OpenAI-compatible SDK (models like openai/gpt-4o, anthropic/claude-3.5-haiku). Returns the project's Model Gateway OpenRouter key, seeded with $1 of AI credits; usage bills per OpenRouter token pricing on that key.

methods.name: insforge.secrets_list
methods.description: List your backend's secrets/keys (names + metadata; values are not returned). FREE (control-plane / metadata).

methods.name: insforge.get
methods.description: Escape hatch: GET any backend API path under /api. Path param is the sub-path (e.g. "database/tables", "storage/config"); extra fields become query params. Covers endpoints not given a dedicated method. Cost depends on the endpoint — see insforge.help.

methods.name: insforge.post
methods.description: Escape hatch: POST any backend API path under /api. Path param is the sub-path; the rest of the payload is sent as the JSON body. Covers endpoints not given a dedicated method. Cost depends on the endpoint.

listing.tagline: The agent-native cloud — your own backend in one call
listing.app_description:
**InsForge** is the agent-native cloud infrastructure platform — the cloud a coding agent drives end to end. This app puts a full InsForge backend behind one Pilot handshake.

`insforge.signup` provisions your OWN isolated InsForge project in a single call — no email, no browser, no human step — via Pilot's signup broker (which holds one managed InsForge account and mints a fresh project per Pilot identity). You immediately get:

- **Postgres database** — tables + PostgREST-style CRUD (`db_create_table`, `db_query`, `db_insert`, `db_update`, `db_delete`) and raw SQL (`db_sql`).
- **Authentication** — users, sessions, OAuth/JWT (`auth_config`, `auth_list_users`).
- **S3-style storage** — buckets + objects (`storage_create_bucket`, `storage_upload`, `storage_download`, `storage_list_objects`).
- **Edge functions** — Deno/TypeScript (`functions_list`, `function_invoke`).
- **AI Model Gateway** — an OpenRouter key seeded with **$1 of AI credits** (`ai_gateway_key`), OpenAI-compatible.
- **Escape hatches** — `insforge.get` / `insforge.post` reach any backend endpoint.

The adapter caches your backend URL + key to `secrets.json`; every method then talks directly to your own backend, authenticated as you. **Free to provision** — you pay only for the resources your backend actually uses. Per-method costs are stated on each method and summarised in `insforge.help`; full pricing at https://insforge.dev/pricing.

Free-tier allowances (per backend): 500 MB Postgres, 1 GB storage, 5 GB bandwidth, 50,000 monthly active users, 100,000 edge-function calls, and $1 of Model Gateway AI credits.
